content.value_statement: Teams lose time when issue titles, labels, and project metadata vary across repositories. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through consistent GitHub issue creation.
actual_capabilities: Validates issue titles against project naming conventions.
Recommends type, priority, scope, and branch labels.
Drafts structured issue bodies with acceptance criteria.
Checks local context for scope, milestones, and project boards.
Provides helper commands for labels, milestones, projects, and issue creation.
Plans parent, blocking, and related issue relationships.
limitations: Live GitHub actions require the GitHub CLI and an authenticated account.
Project-specific rules must exist in local files or repository metadata.
It should request confirmation before creating or changing GitHub issues.
It does not replace product, security, or release-owner review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Issues
use_cases.description: Apply title, label, and body conventions before issues enter a team backlog.

use_cases.title: Prepare Feature Backlogs
use_cases.description: Turn feature plans into scoped issues with priorities, milestones, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Issue Metadata
use_cases.description: Review existing issue drafts and identify missing scope, priority, or project context.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Title
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this issue title for our conventions: "[BUG] Login fails". Suggest a better title and labels.

prompt_templates.title: Draft One Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a GitHub issue for adding export support. Include title, labels, priority, scope, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Review Metadata
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a prepared issue before creation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this issue draft for missing labels, milestone, project board, and relationship context before I create it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Linked Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a parent issue and three child issues for a new authentication flow. Ask before creating anything in GitHub.

output_examples.output: Suggested title: Add dark mode support. Use the feature label, then add priority and scope labels.

output_examples.input: Create an issue for fixing slow search results
output: Title: Improve search result response time.
Recommended labels: bug or enhancement, priority:medium, and the matching scope label.
Acceptance criteria should cover latency target, tests, and regression checks.

output_examples.input: Plan issues for a new billing workflow
output_examples.output: Create one parent tracking issue, then child issues for data model, API flow, UI states, and documentation.

best_practices: Confirm repository, project board, milestone, and scope before creating issues.
Use labels for type and priority instead of title prefixes.
Write acceptance criteria that define completion and verification steps.
anti_patterns: Creating issues before confirming scope, project board, or parent-child relationships.
Using vague titles such as Fix bug or Update code.
Adding multiple type labels when one primary type is required.

faq.question: Does this skill create GitHub issues automatically?
faq.answer: It can provide helper commands and scripts. Users should confirm before any GitHub issue is created or changed.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What labels does it require?
faq.answer: It expects one type label, one priority label, and at least one scope label.

faq.question: Can it assign project boards and milestones?
faq.answer: Yes, when project and milestone context is available and the user confirms the action.

faq.question: Does it validate issue titles?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for type prefixes, vague wording, length concerns, and action-oriented phrasing.

faq.question: What setup is required for live GitHub actions?
faq.answer: The GitHub CLI must be installed and authenticated for the target repository.
